senses.d: Spun wool; woolen thread; also, thread of other material, as of cotton, flax, hemp, or silk; material spun and prepared for use in weaving, knitting, manufacturing sewing thread, or the like.
One of the threads of which the strands of a rope are composed.
A story told by a sailor for the amusement of his companions; a story or tale; as, to spin a yarn.

Yarn.etym: [OE. yarn, ”arn, AS. gearn; akin to D. garen, G., OHG., Icel., Sw., & Dan. garn; of uncertain origin. Cf. Cord.]

senses.d: an old method of printing the article the (AS. þe), the “y” being used in place of the Anglo-Saxon thorn (þ). It is sometimes incorrectly pronounced yē. See The, and Thorn, n., 4.
The plural of the pronoun of the second person in the nominative case.
q: Ye ben to me right welcome heartily.
But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified.
This would cost you your life in case ye were a man.
Vain pomp and glory of this world, I hate ye.
I come, kind gentlemen, strange news to tell ye.

Ye.etym: [OE. ye, ”e, nom. pl., AS. ge, gī; cf. OS. ge, gī, OFries. gī, ī, D. gij, Dan. & Sw. i, Icel. ēr, OHG. ir, G. ihr, Goth. jus, Lith. jus, Gr. υμεἱ̑σ, Skr. yuyam. √189.]

senses.d: Yea; yes.
Yes; ay; a word expressing assent, or an affirmative, or an affirmative answer to a question, now superseded by yes. See Yes.
q: Let your communication be yea, yea; nay, nay.

senses.d: More than this; not only so, but; — used to mark the addition of a more specific or more emphatic clause. Cf. Nay, adv., 2.
q: I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.

Yea.etym: [OE. ye, ya, ”e, ”a, AS. geá; akin to OFries. gē, iē, OS., D., OHG., G., Dan. & Sw. ja, Icel, jā, Goth. ja, jai, and probably to Gr. ἡ̑ truly, verily. √188. Cf. Yes.]

senses.d: An affirmative vote; one who votes in the affirmative; as, a vote by yeas and nays.

The time of the apparent revolution of the sun trough the ecliptic; the period occupied by the earth in making its revolution around the sun, called the astronomical year; also, a period more or less nearly agreeing with this, adopted by various nations as a measure of time, and called the civil year; as, the common lunar year of 354 days, still in use among the Mohammedans; the year of 360 days, etc. In common usage, the year consists of 365 days, and every fourth year (called bissextile, or leap year) of 366 days, a day being added to February on that year, on account of the excess above 365 days (see Bissextile).
q: Of twenty year of age he was, I guess.

senses.d: The time in which any planet completes a revolution about the sun; as, the year of Jupiter or of Saturn.
Age, or old age; as, a man in years.

Year.etym: [OE. yer, yeer, ”er, AS. geár; akin to OFries. i�r, g�r, D. jaar, OHG. jār, G. jahr, Icel. ār, Dan. aar, Sw. år, Goth. j�r, Gr. � a season of the year, springtime, a part of the day, an hour, � a year, Zend yāre year. √4, 279. Cf. Hour, Yore.]

senses.d: Happening, accruing, or coming every year; annual; as, a yearly income; a yearly feast.
Lasting a year; as, a yearly plant.
Accomplished in a year; as, the yearly circuit, or revolution, of the earth.
Annually; once a year to year; as, blessings yearly bestowed.
q: Yearly will I do this rite.

senses.d: To pain; to grieve; to vex.
q: It yearns me not if men my garments wear.

Yearn.etym: [Also earn, ern; probably a corruption of OE. ermen to grieve, AS. ierman, yrman, or geierman, geyrman, fr. earm wretched, poor; akin to D. & G. arm, Icel. armr, Goth. arms. The y- in English is perhaps due to the AS. ge (see Y-).]

senses.d: To be pained or distressed; to grieve; to mourn.
To curdle, as milk.
To be filled with longing desire; to be harassed or rendered uneasy with longing, or feeling the want of a thing; to strain with emotions of affection or tenderness; to long; to be eager.
q: Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother; and he sought where to weep.
Your mother's heart yearns towards you.

Yearn.etym: [OE. yernen, ”ernen, ”eornen, AS. geornian, gyrnan, fr. georn desirous, eager; akin to OS. gern desirous, girnean, gernean, to desire, D. gaarne gladly, willingly, G. gern, OHG. gerno, adv., gern, a., G. gier greed, OHG. girī greed, ger desirous, gerōn to desire, G. begehren, Icel. girna to desire,

senses.d: To cry out, or shriek, with a hideous noise; to cry or scream as with agony or horror.
q: They yelleden as feendes doon in helle.
Nor the night raven, that still deadly yells.
Infernal ghosts and hellish furies round Environed thee; some howled, some yelled.

Yell.etym: [OE. yellen, ”ellen, AS. giellan, gillan, gyllan; akin to D. gillen, OHG. gellan, G. gellen, Icel. gjalla, Sw. gälla to ring, resound, and to AS., OS., & OHG. galan to sing, Icel. gala. Cf. 1st Gale, and Nightingale.]

senses.d: To utter or declare with a yell; to proclaim in a loud tone.
A sharp, loud, hideous outcry.
q: Their hideous yells Rend the dark welkin.

senses.d: Being of a bright saffronlike color; of the color of gold or brass; having the hue of that part of the rainbow, or of the solar spectrum, which is between the orange and the green.
q: Her yellow hair was browded in a tress.
A sweaty reaper from his tillage brought First fruits, the green ear and the yellow sheaf.
The line of yellow light dies fast away.

Yellow.etym: [OE. yelow, yelwe, ”elow, ”eoluw, from AS. geolu; akin to D. geel, OS. & OHG. gelo, G. gelb, Icel. gulr, Sw. gul, Dan. guul, L. helvus light bay, Gr. � young verdure, � greenish yellow, Skr. hari tawny, yellowish. ���. Cf. Chlorine, Gall a bitter liquid, Gold, Yolk.]

senses.d: A bright golden color, reflecting more light than any other except white; the color of that part of the spectrum which is between the orange and green.
A yellow pigment.
To make yellow; to cause to have a yellow tinge or color; to dye yellow.
To become yellow or yellower.
Cowardly; hence, dishonorable; mean; contemptible; as, he has a yellow streak.
Sensational; — said of some newspapers, their makers, etc.; as, yellow journal, journalism, etc.
Ay; yea; — a word which expresses affirmation or consent; — opposed to no.

Yes.etym: [OE. yis, ”is, ”es, ”ise, AS. gese, gise; probably fr. geá yea + swā so. √188. See Yea, and So.]

senses.d: The day last past; the day next before the present.
q: All our yesterdays have lighted fools The way to dusty death.
We are but of yesterday, and know nothing.

senses.d: Fig.: A recent time; time not long past.
q: The proudest royal houses are but of yesterday, when compared with the line of supreme pontiffs.

Yesterday.etym: [OE. ”isterdai, AS. geostran dæg, from geostran, geostra, giestran, gistran, gystran, yesterday (akin to D. gisteren, G. gestern, OHG. gestaron, Icel. gær yesterday, to-morrow, Goth. gistradagis to-morrow, L. heri yesterday, Gr. �, Skr. hyas) + dæg day. Cf. Hestern. ����.]

senses.d: On the day last past; on the day preceding to-day; as, the affair took place yesterday.
The last night; the night last past.
On the last night.
Any one of several species of large marine gastropods belonging to the genus Yetus, or Cymba; a boat shell.
In addition; further; besides; over and above; still.
q: This furnishes us with yet one more reason why our savior, lays such a particular stress acts of mercy.
The rapine is made yet blacker by the pretense of piety and justice.

senses.d: At the same time; by continuance from a former state; still.
q: Facts they had heard while they were yet heathens.

senses.d: Up to the present time; thus far; hitherto; until now; — and with the negative, not yet, not up to the present time; not as soon as now; as, Is it time to go? Not yet. See As yet, under As, conj.
q: Ne never yet no villainy ne said.

senses.d: Before some future time; before the end; eventually; in time.
Even; — used emphatically.
q: Men may not too rashly believe the confessions of witches, nor yet the evidence against them.

Yet.etym: [OE. yet, ”et, ”it, AS. git, gyt, giet, gieta; akin to OFries. ieta, eta, ita, MHG. iezuo, ieze, now, G. jetzo, jetzt.]

senses.d: Nevertheless; notwithstanding; however.
q: Yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

senses.d: To give in return for labor expended; to produce, as payment or interest on what is expended or invested; to pay; as, money at interest yields six or seven per cent.
q: To yelde Jesu Christ his proper rent.
When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength.

senses.d: To furnish; to afford; to render; to give forth.
q: makes milch kine yield blood.
The wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children.

senses.d: To give up, as something that is claimed or demanded; to make over to one who has a claim or right; to resign; to surrender; to relinquish; as a city, an opinion, etc.
q: And, force perforce, I'll make him yield the crown.
Shall yield up all their virtue, all their fame.

senses.d: To admit to be true; to concede; to allow.
q: I yield it just, said Adam, and submit.

senses.d: To permit; to grant; as, to yield passage.
To give a reward to; to bless.
q: Tend me to-night two hours, I ask no more, And the gods yield you for 't.
God yield thee, and God thank ye.

Yield.etym: [OE. yelden, ”elden, ”ilden, AS. gieldan, gildan, to pay, give, restore, make an offering; akin to OFries. jelda, OS. geldan, D. gelden to cost, to be worth, G. gelten, OHG. geltan to pay, restore, make an offering, be worth, Icel. gjalda to pay, give up, Dan. gielde to be worth, Sw. gälla to be wor

senses.d: To give up the contest; to submit; to surrender; to succumb.
q: He saw the fainting Grecians yield.

senses.d: To comply with; to assent; as, I yielded to his request.
To give way; to cease opposition; to be no longer a hindrance or an obstacle; as, men readily yield to the current of opinion, or to customs; the door yielded.
q: Will ye relent, And yield to mercy while 't is offered you?

senses.d: To give place, as inferior in rank or excellence; as, they will yield to us in nothing.
q: Nay tell me first, in what more happy fields The thistle springs, to which the lily yields?

senses.d: Amount yielded; product; — applied especially to products resulting from growth or cultivation.
Inclined to give way, or comply; flexible; compliant; accommodating; as, a yielding temper.
A bar or frame of wood by which two oxen are joined at the heads or necks for working together.
q: A yearling bullock to thy name shall smoke, Untamed, unconscious of the galling yoke.

senses.d: A frame or piece resembling a yoke, as in use or shape.
Fig.: That which connects or binds; a chain; a link; a bond connection.
q: Boweth your neck under that blissful yoke . . . Which that men clepeth spousal or wedlock.
This yoke of marriage from us both remove.

senses.d: A mark of servitude; hence, servitude; slavery; bondage; service.
q: Our country sinks beneath the yoke.
My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

senses.d: Two animals yoked together; a couple; a pair that work together.
q: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them.

senses.d: The quantity of land plowed in a day by a yoke of oxen.
A portion of the working day; as, to work two yokes, that is, to work both portions of the day, or morning and afternoon.

Yoke.etym: [OE. yok, ”oc, AS. geoc; akin to D. juk, OHG. joh, G. joch, Icel. & Sw. ok, Dan. aag, Goth. juk, Lith. jungas, Russ. igo, L. jugum, Gr. ζύγον, Skr. yuga, and to L. jungere to join, Gr. �, Skr. yui. √109, 280. Cf. Join, Jougs, Joust, Jugular, Subjugate, Syzygy, Yuga, Zeugma.]

senses.d: To put a yoke on; to join in or with a yoke; as, to yoke oxen, or pair of oxen.
To couple; to join with another.
q: Cassius, you are yoked with a lamb.

senses.d: To enslave; to bring into bondage; to restrain; to confine.
q: Then were they yoked with garrisons.
The words and promises that yoke The conqueror are quickly broke.

senses.d: To be joined or associated; to be intimately connected; to consort closely; to mate.
q: We 'll yoke together, like a double shadow.

senses.d: A clamp or similar piece that embraces two other parts to hold or unite them in their respective or relative positions, as a strap connecting a slide valve to the valve stem, or the soft iron block or bar permanently connecting the pole pieces of an electromagnet, as in a dynamo.
An associate or companion in, or as in; a mate; a fellow; especially, a partner in marriage.
q: The two languages became yokefellows in a still more intimate manner.
Those who have most distinguished themselves by railing at the sex, very often choose one of the most worthless for a companion and yokefellow.

senses.d: Furious; mad; angry; fierce.

Yond.etym: [Cf. AS. anda, onda, anger, andian to be angry.]

senses.d: Yonder.

Yond.etym: [OE. yond, ”ond, ”eond, through, beyond, over, AS. geond, adv. & prep.; cf. Goth. jaind thither. √188. See Yon, a.]

senses.d: At a distance, but within view.
q: Yonder are two apple women scolding.

Yonder.etym: [OE. yonder, ”onder; cf. OD. ginder, Goth. jaindr� there. ����. See Yond, adv.]

senses.d: Being at a distance within view, or conceived of as within view; that or those there; yon.
q: Yonder men are too many for an embassage.

senses.d: The pronoun of the second person, in the nominative, dative, and objective case, indicating the person or persons addressed. See the Note under Ye.
q: Ye go to Canterbury; God you speed.
Good sir, I do in friendship counsel you To leave this place.
In vain you tell your parting lover You wish fair winds may waft him over.

You.etym: [OE. you, eou, eow, dat. & acc., AS. eów, used as dat. & acc. of ge, gē, ye; akin to OFries. iu, io, D. u, G. euch, OHG. iu, dat., iuwih, acc., Icel. yðr, dat. & acc., Goth. izwis; of uncertain origin. √189. Cf. Your.]

senses.d: Not long born; still in the first part of life; not yet arrived at adolescence, maturity, or age; not old; juvenile; — said of animals; as, a young child; a young man; a young fawn.
q: For he so young and tender was of age.
“Whom the gods love, die young,” has been too long carelessly said; . . . whom the gods love, live young forever.

senses.d: Being in the first part, pr period, of growth; as, a young plant; a young tree.
q: While the fears of the people were young.

senses.d: Having little experience; inexperienced; unpracticed; ignorant; weak.
q: Come, come, elder brother, you are too young in this.

Young.etym: [OE. yung, yong, ”ong, ”ung, AS. geong; akin to OFries. iung, iong, D. joing, OS., OHG., & G. jung, Icel. ungr, Sw. & Dan. ung, Goth. juggs, Lith. jaunas, Russ. iunuii, L. juvencus, juvenis, Skr. juvaça, juvan. √281. Cf. Junior, Juniper, Juvenile, Younker, Youth.]

senses.d: The offspring of animals, either a single animal or offspring collectively.
q: bursting with kindly rupture, forth disclosed Their callow young.

senses.d: The form of the possessive case of the personal pronoun you.

Your.etym: [OE. your, ”our, eowr, eower, AS. eówer, originally used as the gen. of ge, gē, ye; akin to OFries. iuwer your, OS. iuwar, D. uw, OHG. iuwēr, G. euer, Icel. yðar, Goth. izwara, izwar, and E. you. √189. See You.]

senses.d: The quality or state of being young; youthfulness; juvenility.
q: Such as in his face Youth smiled celestial.

senses.d: The part of life that succeeds to childhood; the period of existence preceding maturity or age; the whole early part of life, from childhood, or, sometimes, from infancy, to manhood.
q: He wondered that your lordship Would suffer him to spend his youth at home.
Those who pass their youth in vice are justly condemned to spend their age in folly.

senses.d: A young person; especially, a young man.
q: Seven youths from Athens yearly sent.

senses.d: Young persons, collectively.
q: It is fit to read the best authors to youth first.

Youth.etym: [OE. youthe, youhþe, ”uheðe, ”uweðe, ”eo”eðe, AS. geoguð, geogoð; akin to OS. jugð, D. jeugd, OHG. jugund, G. jugend, Goth. junda. √281. See Young.]

senses.d: Not yet mature or aged; young.
Of or pertaining to the early part of life; suitable to early life; as, youthful days; youthful sports.
Fresh; vigorous, as in youth.
q: After millions of millions of ages . . . still youthful and flourishing.
